title: Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery
synopsis: The SJC found Marshall's complaint judicially out of order on two grounds: that objections raised during a pending judicial case should be reserved for appeal rather than complaint (BCO 32-14; 42-3), and that no complaint is allowable in a judicial case in which an appeal is pending (BCO 43-1). synopsis: Carl Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension: A multi-year judicial dispute concerning the ordination of TE Kurt Lutjens of Ascension Presbytery. The complainants challenged Presbytery's acceptance of Lutjens' modified positions on Lord's Supper invitation requirements, baptism, and women deacons. The commission denied all major specifications, finding that Lutjens' views had substantially changed to conform with church standards, and that the Presbytery's response to a General Assembly exception was properly grounded in fact and pastoral concern, though procedurally imperfect in attempting to clarify prior minutes.

The 15th GA appointed a special committee to inspect all written records and investigate, to report back to the 16th General Assembly. No decision rendered at 15th GA.

canonical_title: Morse v. Covenant Presbytery
title: Morse v. Covenant Presbytery
synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission addressed three issues regarding actions of Covenant Presbytery involving TE Daniel R. Morse and Grace Presbyterian Church. The Commission ruled that teaching elders Morse and Crenshaw, having renounced communion with the PCA by joining the Reformed Episcopal Church, should be removed from presbytery rolls under BCO 38-3. The Commission found no provision requiring churches to notify presbytery before withdrawing from the PCA. Finally, the Commission determined that receiving and recording a protest is an administrative act, not a judicial decision, and that complaints regarding such actions are barred by BCO 45-5.

canonical_title: Hopper v. James River Presbytery
title: Hopper v. James River Presbytery
topics: extraordinary gifts of the Holy Spirit
peace and purity of the church
synopsis: Robert D. Hopper, pastor of Grace Covenant Church in Williamsburg, Virginia, challenged James River Presbytery's April 1991 action forbidding him from preaching and teaching views affirming that the extraordinary gifts of the Holy Spirit (including prophecy and tongues) may be present in the church in the present age. The Standing Judicial Commission denied the complaint, holding that presbytery has constitutional authority under BCO 13-9 and 34-5 to restrict teaching and preaching when it determines such views may be harmful to the spiritual welfare of the churches under its care, and that such restriction does not violate liberty of conscience absent a determination that the forbidden teaching is heretical.

The SJC confirmed this action, finding that the Commission appointed as Interim Session was the proper court of original jurisdiction and remanding the complaints for adjudication by that Commission.

synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission affirmed that Presbytery of Western Carolina did not err in conducting its BCO 31-2 investigation of accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley or in finding no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC found no constitutional error in Presbytery's procedures and gave great deference to the lower court's discretionary judgment, noting that BCO 31-2 does not mandate specific procedures for investigations. The SJC also held that complainants Kirk Lyons and Robert Woodward lacked standing to bring complaints under BCO 43-1 and 11-4.

Also alleged error in the not guilty verdict. SJC ruled error in procedures and instructed new trial. Issue: Did the
title: Complaint: TE Art Sartorius vs. Siouxlands Presbytery 2013-03 Complaint: Mr. G. Rick Marshall vs. Pacific Presbytery 2013-06 Appeal: TE Stephen Gonzales vs. Great Lakes Presbytery 2013-08 Complaint of
topics: rules of evidence in ecclesiastical courts
synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Art Sartorius and six others against Presbytery of Siouxlands, finding that the Presbytery erred when it approved its Judicial Commission's verdict acquitting TE Gregory Lawrence of five charges related to Federal Vision theology and unconventional views on baptism and apostasy. The SJC identified serious procedural errors, specifically that the Judicial Commission admitted exculpatory post-indictment written statements from the defendant without subjecting them to cross-examination, contrary to BCO 35-5. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial with detailed instructions regarding evidence procedures and Presbytery oversight.

canonical_title: Request for Reference from Blue Ridge Presbytery
title: Request for Reference from Blue Ridge Presbytery
synopsis: Blue Ridge Presbytery requested that the Standing Judicial Commission hear and decide a complaint because of claimed bias and constitutional questions. The SJC denied the request for reference, holding that the record did not demonstrate affirmative bias, serious division, constitutional questions, or delicate issues that would warrant reference under BCO 41-2. The presbytery was directed to hear and decide the complaint itself.

canonical_title: Oxbalt et al. v. Pacific Presbytery
title: Oxbalt et al. v. Pacific Presbytery
synopsis: RE Sean Ozbalt and RE Erin Barr filed complaints challenging Pacific Presbytery's handling of TE Rankin Wilbourne's case. The SJC sustained the complaints, finding that the reading of a judicial commission report not agreed upon by the accused violated BCO 38-1, that the sins were not base and flagitious, and that procedural constitutional violations occurred. The SJC annulled the censure of deposition and recommended treating the 17-month censure as a definite suspension from office.

title: BCO 40-5 Matter re Metropolitan NY. Decided 01/12/24. Decided, with dissenting opinions
synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission ruled on a matter involving Metropolitan New York Presbytery's handling of a session that permitted a woman to expound Scripture during worship and held services without sermons. The SJC remitted the matter to the Presbytery to complete its work and report to the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records, while critiquing the procedural manner in which the matter was referred to the SJC.

canonical_title: BCO 40-5 Matter re NW Georgia. Decided 01/12/24. Decided
title: BCO 40-5 Matter re NW Georgia. Decided 01/12/24. Decided
synopsis: The SJC, pursuant to citation by the 50th General Assembly under BCO 40-5, found that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred egregiously in approving calls and installing three candidates as associate pastors through a constitutionally deficient election process (slate voting, standing vote, failure to record number of voters present). The SJC stayed all further proceedings and declined to annul the installations, finding no PCA precedent for such relief.
